title: Burst safety latch prevented emergency scale-up; tenant priority desync caused prolonged shortfall
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a late-night traffic spike one of our large Dedicated tenants experienced sustained request rejects and high latency despite available cloud GPUs. The autoscaler did not trigger aggressive scale-up because a safety latch vetoed scaling while a transient topology update was in flight. Simultaneously, tenant priority labels were out of sync between the routing layer and the autoscaler leader due to a delayed key-value reconciliation, which prevented the tenant from being granted burst headroom. This resulted in ~42 minutes of degraded throughput for three enterprise customers and several escalations to support.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial report from SRE: multiple customer complaints at 02:13 UTC showing token-level 429s for dedicated tenants. On-call pulled emergency runbook and opened investigation. Linked dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/allocs/spike-2025-02-12

2025-02-12 - Marco Chen: Reproduced in staging: trigger synthetic burst and observed scale decision was blocked by safety_latch=true in scale-controller logs. Safety latch memo shows recent topology_change_timestamp=2025-02-12T02:12:45Z. Attach: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/413

2025-02-12 - SRE (Lia Gomes): Found routing->autoscaler label delta: tenant.priority label for tenant AcmeHealth was not propagated to leader because reconciliation loop had backoff due to transient 503 from config-service. Logged: config-service/err-503-2025-02-12.log

2025-02-12 - Marco Chen: Hotfix idea: allow bypass of safety latch when (queued_requests > 200 && sustained_qps_growth > 2x 30s) and require canary rollout. Implemented prototype branch 'bypass-safety-on-backlog' (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/417).

2025-02-13 - Ops (Jon Rivera): Deployed canary to us-west1 reserved pools at 04:00 UTC. Observed immediate scale-up for impacted tenants and queue drain within 6 minutes. Customer slack updates posted to #cust-escalations channel and emailed affected contacts. Temporary mitigation succeeded; customers report resumed normal throughput.

2025-02-13 - Marco Chen: Root cause hypothesis: safety latch semantic is too conservative when topology updates coincide with config propagation delays. Secondary cause: label reconciliation backoff extended label-staleness window causing priority misclassification. Proposed full fix: (1) tighten topology-update detection to use commit-marker instead of timestamp staleness, (2) add eventual-consistency-aware label snapshot for scale decisions, (3) augment telemetry and SLOs to alert on queue-backlog-triggered bypass events.

2025-02-13 - Product (Nina Basu): Raised customer comms template and compensation options for enterprise customers. Draft PRD for 'priority reconciliation watchdog' created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/PRDs/priority-watchdog

2025-02-14 - Marco Chen: Merged hotfix to main with feature flag 'bypass_safety_on_backlog' default off. Release plan: enable to 10% of Dedicated pools for 24h, observe scale decisions and false-positive rates. Post-deploy checklist in repo. Endpoint: release notes - autoscaler-2.3.1-hotfix

2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Follow-ups: add unit+integration tests for safety latch bypass, add a dashboard (metric: safety_latch_bypass_count, bypass_success_rate, stalled_label_reconciliations), and schedule postmortem review with SRE, Runtime, and Routing teams in Cycle 2025-W09. Assigned action owners in follow-up doc.

Action items: 1) Stability - implement commit-marker logic (owner: Marco Chen, estimate 5). 2) Label reconciliation watchdog (owner: SRE team, estimate 3). 3) Telemetry + alerts (owner: Observability eng, estimate 2). 4) Customer comms and SLA review (owner: Nina Basu, due 2025-02-18).
